1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons; and wherein the weapons stores processor panel receives and processes interlock signals from the flight management system prior to enabling generation of fire signals.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard; and wherein the weapons stores processor panel further communicates with avionics equipment via an avionics interface bus configured in accordance with MIL-STD-1553.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel; wherein the laser pointer is controlled by the weapons stores processor panel to improve targeting accuracy of aircraft weapons.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display; wherein the data concentrator unit processes signals from the weapons stores processor panel and the flight management system.

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position; wherein the master arm switch controls power distribution and fire signal generation through the weapons stores processor panel.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals to the weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction display; wherein the display information is generated based on interlock status and weapons store configuration data.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons; wherein the weapons stores processor panel coordinates with the weapons bus controller to enforce safety interlocks before enabling weapons firing.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel; wherein the laser pointer is controlled by the weapons stores processor panel to improve targeting accuracy of the aircraft weapon.
